title: Low-degree concentrating Fourier family
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $\varepsilon$ be real. Define the low-degree $L^1$-concentrating Fourier family of $f$ at degree $k$ and tolerance $\varepsilon$ to be the $L^1$-concentrating Fourier family of the degree-$k$ low-degree part of $f$, with tolerance $\varepsilon/4$.
hypotheses_covered: real-valued function f on the n-dimensional sign cube
caveat: The supplied context does not define the low-degree part or the L1-concentrating Fourier family, so this records the construction in terms of those named objects.
